title: Privacy policy
summary: What the app stores, where it lives, and how to delete it.
body:
Recovery Log is a private diary of your surgical recovery. This policy says what it stores, where it lives, who can see it, and how to get rid of it.

The app is provided by [[CONTROLLER: legal name and address]].

WHAT IT STORES:

Your account. Your email address, which is how you sign in. Your first name, last name and date of birth, which is what someone joining your care team types to confirm they are joining the right person's log.

Your surgery. The procedure, your surgeon, the date and time, your surgeon's office phone number, the temperature you count as a fever, and any notes you add.

Your days. One record for each day you log: the day number, when you woke, how long you slept and in what position, and your answers to the daily red flag check, including anything you wrote about what happens next.

Your entries. One record for each entry: its date, its time, its type and the values that type asks for. Which types those are is up to you. They can include check-in scores such as pain, water, meals, nutrients, medicines and doses, temperature, rest, movement, bowel movements, urine colour, drainage, incision findings marked on a body map, compression garments, skin changes, manual lymphatic drainage, body work, vibration plate and compression pump sessions, body measurements, weight, and photographs.

Your lists. The garments you wear, the medication groups you take, and the places you measure.

That is all of it. The app builds no profile of you, does not track you across other apps or websites, and carries no advertising.

WHY IT STORES IT:

To show you your own log, to total it up, and to produce the PDF you hand to your surgeon. That is the entire purpose. Your log is not analysed for anything else and is not used to train anything.

WHERE IT LIVES:

Recovery Log is built on Base44, which hosts the app and stores its data on our instructions in order to run it. Photographs you add are uploaded to Base44's file storage.

WHAT LEAVES THE APP:

Two things, and only these.

When you search for a medicine by name, the letters you type are sent to RxNav, the free drug name service run by the United States National Library of Medicine, to find matching names. Nothing about you or your log goes with that request, and nothing is sent unless you use the search.

When you export your log, the PDF is built on your device and goes wherever you send it.

WHO CAN SEE YOUR LOG:

You, and the people you invite to your care team. Nobody else. Inviting and removing care team members is yours to do, at any time, in Profile. Removing someone ends their access immediately.

HOW LONG IT IS KEPT:

Until you delete it.

DELETING IT:

Profile has Delete my account. It asks you to type your email address, and then it is permanent, with no undo.

If you are the patient it removes the whole log: every entry, every day, every surgery, your measurements, your garments, your medication groups, your care team's access, and your login.

If you are on someone's care team it removes your login and your access. The patient's log is untouched.

WHAT YOU CAN DO:

See everything the app holds about you, because the app is that record and Profile exports it as a PDF.

Correct anything, by editing the entry or the surgery it belongs to.

Delete all of it, permanently, from Profile.

CHILDREN:

Recovery Log is not intended for anyone under [[MINIMUM AGE]].

CHANGES:

If this policy changes you will be asked to read and accept the new version the next time you open the app. Which version you accepted, and when, is kept on your account.

CONTACT:

[[CONTACT: name and email for privacy questions]]

[[LEGAL: this draft states what the code actually does. It makes no claim about which statutory framework applies. The GDPR lawful basis, UK and EU representatives, CCPA and other state disclosures, retention periods stated in time rather than in "until you delete it", and any HIPAA analysis are yours to add.]]

title: Permissions
summary: What the app asks your phone for, and what it never asks for.
body:
Recovery Log asks your phone for very little. This is the whole list.

PHOTOS AND CAMERA:

Asked for when you add a photo to an entry, and not before.

Used to attach that photo to that entry in your log.

The photo is uploaded to the app's storage, so it is there when you open your log on another device and so it appears in your exported PDF.

If you say no, every other tracker still works. You just cannot attach photos.

VIBRATION:

A short buzz when you tap a tracker button, so you know it registered. There is no permission prompt for this. Turn off haptics in your phone's settings to silence it.

STORAGE ON THIS DEVICE:

The app remembers two things in your browser: whether you chose light, dark or system appearance, and which surgery you had open. Nothing from your log is kept there.

WHAT IT NEVER ASKS FOR:

Location. Contacts. Microphone. Calendar. Bluetooth. Notifications.

The app does not read anything from Apple Health or Google Fit, and does not write anything to them.

title: Personal information and sharing
summary: What identifies you, who sees it, and who never does.
body:
WHAT IS PERSONALLY IDENTIFYING:

Directly identifying. Your email address, your first and last name, your date of birth, and any photograph you add.

Identifying in combination. Your surgery date, your procedure, your surgeon's name and office phone number, your measurements and your weight.

Health information. Everything else in the log: pain and the other check-in scores, medicines and doses, temperature, incision findings, drainage, bowel movements, urine colour, and the rest. This is health information about you, and it is the most sensitive thing the app holds.

WHO IT IS SHARED WITH:

Your care team, and only people you invite yourself. You invite them by email address in Profile, and they get in only if they can also confirm your first name, last name and date of birth. A care team member sees the whole log for the patient who invited them. You can make a member read only, and you can remove any member at any time, which ends their access immediately.

Base44, which hosts the app and stores its data on our instructions and does not use it for anything else.

The United States National Library of Medicine, and only this: when you search for a medicine by name, the letters you type go to its free RxNav drug name service. No name, no email, no account identifier and nothing from your log goes with it.

Anyone you hand an export to. The PDF is yours. Once you send it, where it goes is up to you.

WHO IT IS NOT SHARED WITH:

It is not sold. It is not shared with advertisers, data brokers or analytics companies. It is not shared with insurers or employers. It is not used to train any model. There is no advertising or third party analytics code in the app.

WHAT YOU CONTROL:

Who is on your care team, and whether each of them can write or only read.

What you log. Every tracker can be turned off in Profile. Turning one off hides its button and keeps what you already logged.

Getting a copy, as a PDF, from Profile.

Getting rid of all of it, permanently, from Profile.

[[LEGAL: this app holds health information a patient enters about themselves and shares it with people that patient invites. Whether that makes it a HIPAA covered entity or a business associate, and which state health privacy laws reach it, is a question for you rather than a claim this document makes.]]
